claim: Morin made repeated Paris weather observations; modern researchers interpret early nonstandard measurements. The record shows severe cold interrupted by milder periods.
locator: Morin methods and historical measurements; Météo-France opening weather sections
limit: No invented thermometer scale or unsupported numeric graph; use categorical sequence only.

checked.method: source passages read, wording compared, refutation attempted
checked.evidence: Météo-France: Louis Morin kept temperature readings 'trois ou quatre fois par jour, du 1er février 1665 au 13 juillet 1716'; the raw data 'doivent donc être retravaillées' because zero point, degree value and instrument were undefined. Pliemon et al. 2022 abstract: measurements digitised from copies of Morin's originals and subjected to quality analysis; 'apart from small inhomogeneities, reliable'; winter 1708/09 devastating in consecutive ice days though other winters colder on some measures.
checked.source_locators: SRC02 first interview answer; SRC03 abstract
checked.refutation: Checked that the script never gives a modern Celsius value as Morin's own reading and never calls 1709 the coldest ever; it does not. Holds.
checked.reviewer: Claude acting for the director (owner delegation 2026-10-09)
